class.name: PhysXWaterMist3D
class.brief_description: Mist from falling or breaking water, drawn in raster and under path tracing.
class.description: The finest drops a waterfall, a rapid or a fountain throws (about [member drop_radius] 20 um): they settle at a few cm/s (Stokes) and evaporate in seconds to minutes depending on the humidity, so they ride the air. A small grid of liquid water content (g/m³) over a box aligned with the world axes, stepped on the CPU at [member update_rate]: semi-Lagrangian advection (Stam 1999), turbulent [member diffusion], settling and evaporation. Mist is added at the source box and carried by the source's own air, a wall jet leaving the source along [member jet_direction] at [member jet_speed] and spreading round it (the spray wind a fall drags down), plus the wind of the active [code]WeatherMap3D[/code] (or [member wind]). Raster: a [FogVolume] over the box with the grid as its [member FogMaterial.density_texture]; while a mist is live and the [Environment]'s volumetric fog is off, the mist turns it on with no fog of its own ([member Environment.volumetric_fog_density] 0), lit by the sky ([member Environment.volumetric_fog_ambient_inject] 1) and reaching 200 m, and puts it back when the last mist goes. Path tracing: a dense medium traced with delta tracking like simulated gas, extinction 3 LWC / (2 rho_w r), single scattering albedo 0.999 and a Henyey-Greenstein lobe of g 0.85 (drops this size scatter forward). Up to five mists are traced at once; a frame where a [code]PhysXFlow3D[/code] traces its gas shows that instead. [PhysXRiver3D] makes one at the foot of each waterfall ([member PhysXRiver3D.fall_mist]).

method.name: advance
method.description: Steps the grid [param seconds] ahead now, as if that much time had passed.

method.name: get_max_density
method.description: The densest cell's liquid water content, g/m³.

method.name: sample_density
method.description: Liquid water content (g/m³) at a world position, 0 outside the box.

members.member: Grid cell size, m; grown so no side holds more than 64 cells.
Turbulent diffusivity of the air, m²/s.
Drop radius, micrometres: sets how fast the mist settles, how long it lasts and how much light it stops per gram.
Off, no more mist is added; what is there drifts off and evaporates.
Take the wind and the humidity from the active [code]WeatherMap3D[/code], when there is one.
Relative humidity without a [code]WeatherMap3D[/code]: drops of 20 um last about 13 s at 0.85, a minute at 0.97.
Local, horizontal: the way the source's air leaves it. It spreads round this direction but never goes back against it.
Speed of the source's air as it leaves the source, m/s, falling off as it spreads.
The box, m: centred on the node in x and z, from the node up, along the world axes.
Half extents of the source box, in the node's axes.
Centre of the source box, local.
Grams of mist added a second.
